question: Rani has borrowed an amount of ₹2,00,000 from a bank to start a business. How much simple interest will she pay at a rate of 7% per annum after 2 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest** percentage = Rate × Time

Total % = 7% × 2 = 14%

Interest = 14% of ₹2,00,000 = 14 × 2000 = ₹28,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fdc95582872594df150c4a448c0811fc894378f2020363355bf2e364a93666bb.png] 

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹2,00,000

**Rate (R)** = 7% per annum

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (2,00,000 × 7 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 2,000 × 14

⇒ SI = 28,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) to be paid after the time period is calculated as **Amount = Principal + Simple Interest**.

Constant Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest amount remains **constant** every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Rate and Time Units

Ensure that the **Rate** and **Time** are in the same time units (e.g., if Rate is per annum, Time must be in years).
